findings.title: upsampled_count uses sum(sample_weight) with no NULL handling
findings.body: The new aggregate is `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. Events stored before `sample_weight` was populated, or without a client sample rate, have NULL in that column. `sum` skips NULLs, so those events are counted as 0, or the whole bucket becomes NULL and `toInt64` then yields 0 or an error. Allowlisted projects therefore show undercounted or zeroed error charts as soon as their data contains any unweighted events. The comment says the schema guarantees the column exists, but a nullable column existing does not mean it is populated. It should be `sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))` so unweighted events count as 1. Also, the function is registered as a public (non-private) discover function. Users can call `upsampled_count()` directly, including on datasets or event types where `sample_weight` does not exist.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses the outer `dataset` and request query instead of the scoped dataset and actual query
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` takes `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check passes the closed-over endpoint-level `dataset`. The check also reads `request.GET['query']` instead of the `query` argument. In the dashboard-widget split path, the code calls `_get_event_stats(discover, ..., f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction")` or `scoped_dataset` with a modified query. The decision is still based on the original dataset (for example `metrics_enhanced_performance`, which returns False) and the original request string. The same widget can then get upsampled counts in one branch and raw counts in another. The split-decision logic compares `error_results` against `original_results`, which can come out inconsistent. The decision should be computed from `scoped_dataset` and the `query` actually being executed.

findings.title: Substring match on 'event.type:error' misclassifies negated and compound queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True if the raw lowercase query string contains `event.type:error`. That matches `!event.type:error` (the opposite intent), `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and any query where the text appears inside a longer token or value. In those cases `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` over transaction or other non-error rows, which have no sample weight. The result is wrong counts or Snuba errors. The docstring claims this errs on the side of caution, but a substring match does the opposite. It needs to parse the query, or at least check token boundaries and negation.

findings.title: Cache layer is unnecessary, collision-prone, and never invalidated
findings.body: The allowlist check is an in-process `options.get` followed by an `in` scan. Wrapping it in `cache.get`/`cache.set` (a network round-trip to memcached or redis) is likely slower than the lookup it replaces. It also adds staleness: option changes take up to 60s to apply, and the module's own `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called anywhere. The key is built from `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`, a 64-bit non-cryptographic hash, so two different project sets can collide and share an eligibility result. It is also not independent of the organization's data beyond org id. Joining the sorted ids, or dropping the cache entirely, would be safer.

findings.title: Docstring contradicts the caching behavior
findings.body: The NOTE on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says it reads the allowlist fresh each time so the latest configuration is always used. The caller wraps it in a 60-second cache, so results can be up to a minute stale. Comments in the endpoint make similar claims ("cached result ensures consistent behavior", "most current schema assumptions", "better query optimization and caching") that are not true of the code. They will mislead maintainers about when the allowlist takes effect.

findings.title: Upsampling transform applied in RPC branches that can never be eligible
findings.body: `use_rpc` is only true for `spans_rpc` and `ourlogs`. `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` returns False for every dataset other than errors and discover, so `upsampling_enabled` is always False in the two RPC branches (top-events and timeseries). The `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` calls there are dead code. They also suggest to readers that RPC datasets are supported, and they would feed a non-RPC `upsampled_count() as count` column into the RPC `y_axes` if the gating ever changed.

findings.title: Endpoint tests miss top_events, negated queries, the cache path and the dashboard split path
findings.body: The new tests only cover plain timeseries with `count()`. They do not cover the `topEvents` branch where the transform is also applied. They do not cover `!event.type:error` or compound queries, which the substring check mishandles. They do not cover events with NULL `sample_weight`, the likely failure for `sum(sample_weight)`. They do not cover the dashboard split path, where the outer `dataset` is used instead of the scoped one. The tests also mock `options` while using the real cache, and `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and `invalidate_upsampling_cache` have no direct unit tests. The 60s cache and the unused invalidation are therefore untested.

findings.title: Blanket exception swallowing in test factory helper hides malformed fixtures
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the context lookup and the float conversion in `except Exception: pass`. A malformed `client_sample_rate` (for example a string) is silently ignored and the event is stored without `sample_rate`. The upsampling tests then fail on count assertions rather than at the real cause. The `if client_sample_rate:` check also skips a legitimate rate of 0. Narrow the exceptions or let invalid fixtures fail loudly.

findings.title: Stray submodule gitlink committed to the repository
findings.body: A new `sentry-repo` entry is added as a git submodule pointer (`Subproject commit a5d2909...`, the base commit). It is unrelated to the feature and has no corresponding `.gitmodules` entry, so it looks like an accidental commit of a local checkout. It can break `git submodule` operations and should be removed from the PR.
